finding.title: Valid numeric-overflow provenance input can be re-emitted as nonstandard Infinity in append-only JSONL archive
finding.fixture: Two valid JSONL FlowObservation records with finite value/timestamps; first provenance={'scale':1}, second provenance={'scale':1e309} as literal JSON numeric exponent, distinct source_record_id; run_once(network=False, external_jsonl=[file], as_of_ms=1800000000000). Reverse row order and retry. Python json.loads parses 1e309 as inf.
finding.mechanism: FlowObservation.from_dict copies provenance without finite-value validation; storage._semantic_signature and append_observations json.dumps use default allow_nan=True, so second row can serialize Infinity token, which is not RFC-compliant JSON, while Python's permissive loader may accept it.
oracle_expected_assertions: Archive lines must parse with strict JSON constant rejection; no NaN/Infinity tokens in observations.jsonl.
Overflowed provenance must fail closed before any archive row is admitted, or be explicitly normalized with a documented provenance quality marker.
On rejection, baseline archive and latest/audit_latest/anata_latest must remain one generation; no silent partial admission.
Both permutations, corrected retry, exact duplicate retry and point-in-time provenance preserve deterministic counts and outputs.
finding.primitive_check: isolated Python stdlib json.loads('1e309') -> inf; json.dumps -> Infinity; not an exact-repository test
finding.separate_from: Prior 04:59 TypeError partial-admission isolated 3-pass evidence; this is a distinct silent nonstandard-archive serialization path, not a repeat.
